A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSAM research despite the changed title and formatting. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification and GLUE experiments, numerical toy problems, and analyses of flatness, convergence, and hyperparameter sensitivity.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark/model comparisons, Hessian measurements, sampler-step experiments, and measured runtimes.

M1.justification: The tilted objective, gradient weighting, and approximate HMC-inspired sampler remain unchanged. v1 Algorithm 2 becomes v2 Algorithm 3. The added experiments with multiple HMC steps exercise the already-described N parameter rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds 200-class TinyImageNet classification while retaining CIFAR100, 20%-noisy CIFAR100, DTD, and the same nine GLUE tasks. This is a limited expansion within the existing image-classification coverage; additional architectures are experimental-setting changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ESAM1 and ESAM2 to the GLUE comparison, which previously contained only ERM, SAM, and TSAM. These compute-matched SAM variants were already evaluated on image tasks. The image comparator set remains ERM, SAM, ESAM1, ESAM2, PGN, and RSAM.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands model and training configurations: WideResNet16-8 is evaluated on CIFAR100, noisy CIFAR100, and DTD, including training DTD from scratch; TinyImageNet uses ResNet18 and ResNet34. It also introduces top-five Hessian-eigenvalue measurements and N=2/3 sampler evaluations. The stated hyperparameter settings for retained experiments are largely unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds Hessian-spectrum evidence testing flatness beyond neighborhood loss mean and variance. Appendix C adds a limited HMC-step ablation and runtime comparisons to examine accuracy–computation tradeoffs. Earlier tilt, scheduling, perturbation-count, naive-sampling, and loss-comparison analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 adds apparent uncertainty annotations to image accuracies, such as 77.78 (.1), whereas v1 reports only point estimates. The PDF does not define these parenthesized quantities or provide run/seed counts, so their statistical meaning and whether additional repetitions occurred remain unresolved.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for new model/dataset configurations, GLUE comparators, Hessian spectra, HMC steps, and runtimes. Retained table scores are unchanged after percentage conversion. New TinyImageNet results include TSAM at 73.55 versus RSAM at 73.57 with ResNet18, and TSAM at 77.79 versus PGN at 77.80 with ResNet34; these are new comparisons, not declines from v1.

T1.justification: The principal definitions, assumptions, theorems, generalization inequality, and Appendix B proofs are retained. However, Section 3.3 removes v1's theoretical assertions that SAM's population-risk bound is no smaller than ERM's and larger than finite-t TSAM's, narrowing the stated consequences of the bound.

C1.justification: v2 drops the introduction's explicit contribution claim of a tighter generalization bound than SAM and describes abstract weighting through loss alone. Core smoothness, flatness, and empirical-performance claims remain. The conclusion also omits v1's GLM-class qualification of the flatness guarantee, although Theorem 3.6 retains the restriction.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 changes the claimed implication from obtaining smaller population error to obtaining a smaller upper bound on population error. The new HMC analysis also supports retaining one sampling step because additional steps bring little accuracy benefit at greater computational cost. Existing caveats about sampler consistency and the flatness–generalization relationship remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a stated public-code pointer in Section 5 and training-time information in Appendix C, Table 5. It removes v1's disclosure of V100 GPUs with 32GB memory. Appendix C.1 largely preserves the existing hyperparameter information rather than supplying substantially fuller implementation instructions.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions TSAM as a special case of Tahmasebi et al. (2024), while noting that work did not specifically study TSAM. It adds connections to randomized smoothing, noise-stability optimization, risk-sensitive control, and newer SAM research. These refine the existing positioning around parameter-space exponential tilting.

P1.justification: The title becomes 'Tilted Sharpness-Aware Minimization'; introductory, related-work, and generalization passages receive localized revisions. Appendix C is reorganized, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added. Most of the six-section narrative remains, with a useful correction of Section 5.3's erroneous t=0 description.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout. Table 1 is restructured with dataset/model column groups and expanded comparisons. The training/test-loss table and tilt/scheduling figures move to Appendix C, which gains HMC-step and runtime tables. Existing plots largely retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through additional model/benchmark evaluations, compute-matched GLUE comparisons, and targeted flatness, sampler, and runtime analyses. The code pointer and more cautious interpretation of the generalization bound also help. These gains are incremental: uncertainty annotations remain undefined, hardware information disappears, and the retained blanket superiority claim overlooks the slightly lower TSAM means in two TinyImageNet comparisons.
